How We Rate Canadian Online Casinos

Canadian online casinos you’ll find at Casinomeister always go through our unflinching casino rating process to make sure nothing gets past us. 

We always begin by looking at each Canadian casino’s licensing information. If there’s even a trace of them not doing things by the book, you’ll never see that platform listed here.  

Next, we run our eyes over each Canadian casino’s game selection and the software providers they list. We look for familiar faces such as Evolution Gaming, Pragmatic Play, NetEnt, Yggdrasil, and the like. The more the merrier, and the higher their rating goes.

Then, we weigh up every casino’s promotional offers by rifling through terms and conditions. The more they’re crafted with players’ best interests in mind, the better the score. 

How to Choose the Best Real Money Online Casino in Canada

With so many online casinos all over the map, telling the good from the stuff that’s only decent on paper doesn’t come easy even to the trained eye. But we’re here with some pointers on choosing the best real-money online casino in Canada and not regret your decision.

Make sure they’re properly licensed — Unlicensed casinos aren’t just sketchy, they’re nowhere near the top online casinos in Canada. So, check if they hold a legit license first, run them by regulators, and try not to have anything to do with places that seem to play dirty. 

Check their reputation — Before going for any Canadian gambling site, poke around, see what others have to say on forums, and go over online casino reviews. Sometimes, there’s no better way to find the truth about any casino than hearing what people who’ve been there before have to say. 

Go over their game lineup — A casino’s game and software provider lineup is usually a telltale sign of how good it is. If they’ve joined forces with giants such as Microgaming, NetEnt, Pragmatic Play, and the like, that could be a sign you’re in good hands. 

Canada’s Online Gambling Laws and Regulations

When we take a bird’s eye view of Canadian online gambling laws and regulations, we see them split between federal and provincial control.

Canadian federal regulation (specifically the Criminal Code of Canada) prohibits all types of gambling (including online betting) except when it’s being run and regulated by provincial regulators. What this means in layman’s terms is that private companies cannot just launch a gambling website whenever they feel like it — everything has to pass through provincial regulators. 

Since each province in Canada is governed by a different regulator, the easiest way to wrap our heads around this legal tangle is to lay all the facts out in one place — a well-structured table.

Province	Regulatory body 	Type of gambling allowed	Private operators availability
Ontario	Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO), iGaming Ontario (iGO)	Online casinos, sports betting, lottery, poker, live dealer	Yes, if licensed through iGaming Ontario
Quebec	Loto-Quebec	Online casinos, sports betting, lottery, poker	No, only government-run
British Columbia	Gaming Policy and Enforcement Branch (GPEB), British Columbia Lottery Corporation (BCLC)	Online casinos, sports betting, lottery, poker	No, only government-run
Alberta	Alberta Gaming Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC)	Online casinos, sports betting, lottery	No, only government-run
Manitoba	Liquor, Gaming and Cannabis Authority of Manitoba (LGCA), Manitoba Liquor and Lotteries (MBLL) 	Online casinos, sports betting, lottery	No, only government-run
Saskatchewan	Saskatchewan Liquor and Gaming Authority (SLGA), Saskatchewan Indian Gaming Authority (SIGA)	Online casinos, sports betting, lottery	No, only government-run
New Brunswick	Gaming, Liquor and Security Licensing Branch,  Atlantic Lottery Corporation (ALC)	Online casinos, sports betting, lottery	No, only government-run
Nova Scotia	Alcohol, Gaming, Fuel and Tobacco Division (AGFT), Atlantic Lottery Corporation (ALC)	Online casinos, sports betting, lottery	No, only government-run
Prince Edward Island	Consumer, Corporate and Insurance Division, Atlantic Lottery Corporation (ALC)	Online casinos, sports betting, lottery	No, only government-run
Newfoundland & Labrador	Consumer Affairs Division, Atlantic Lottery Corporation (ALC)	Online casinos, sports betting, lottery	No, only government-run

The only lone wolf to Canada’s provincial regulators is the Kahnawake Gaming Commission, the only gambling regulator operating independently under the Mohawk Territory laws of Kahnawake. Because of this, provincial regulators see KGC-licensed casinos as offshore gambling sites, but that doesn’t mean players from other provinces won’t be able to access them. Players in Ontario, though, are legally restricted from playing at such sites, so if you’re one of them, your best option is to head over to our Ontario online casinos page and make your pick there.

Do any online casinos in Canada pay out instantly?

Instant payouts go hand in hand with crypto, so every Kahnawake-licensed casino that accepts cryptocurrencies, such as Jackpot City, should pay out your winnings instantly.

Are online casinos legal in Canada?

Online casinos are legal in Canada as long as they’re approved and licensed by the province they operate in.

Responsible Gambling

Gambling involves financial risk, so set a budget and time limit before playing and stop if it’s causing you stress or harm. If you or someone you know is seeking help right now, free, confidential support is available 24/7 from the National Gambling Helpline on 0808 8020 133. UK players can also self-exclude from all UKGC-licensed sites via GamStop.co.uk.
